statements.venue: Energy and Commerce Health Subcommittee hearing, opening statement as prepared for delivery
statements.quote: But today, instead of focusing on the concerns that all our constituents have about the destruction of public health in this country, we are holding a broad hearing on AI that was hastily put together as a distraction.
statements.context: As ranking member, she opened a hearing on AI in health care by criticizing the majority for holding it instead of oversight hearings on the Department of Health and Human Services and the CDC.

grade_reason: She has spoken about AI only in a September 2025 health hearing, calling the AI hearing a distraction from public health oversight; no statement about catastrophic AI risk was found in 2025 or 2026.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. The official site press release page (June to October 2026) showed no AI releases; earlier pages were not checked. She is not listed as a cosponsor of H.R. 10538, the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, on fastdemocracy.com (12 cosponsors listed); congress.gov returned 403 so the official list was not checked. Search summaries paraphrased her hearing remarks (AI merits study; AI should augment, not replace, clinicians); these paraphrases come from AI-generated search summaries of trade press (Medical Economics, AMCP update) and were not turned into quotes. A search snippet mentioned a 2026 primary opponent claiming she took campaign money from industries including AI; this is not her statement. Her questioning of witnesses at the 3 September 2025 hearing was not read in the transcript.
